show.summary: Unscripted is the podcast of Nivedkrishna Thavarayil (@tvedukr_12 on Instagram), a creative strategist and director in New York. Every episode is a true story from his work: directing 12+ micro dramas and short docuseries for Canvas, making films in New York on an indie budget, campaigns for Sony Pictures, Netflix India and Zomato, and the content and creator strategy he runs at Thava Studio. Practical lessons on creative strategy, paid and organic social, short-form video, filmmaking and AI video production, with checklists and the mistakes to avoid. Narrated with his own ElevenLabs voice clone.
show.keywords: Nivedkrishna Thavarayil, tvedukr_12, creative strategy, filmmaking, micro dramas, short-form video, social media marketing, New York

how-i-make-films-in-new-york-on-an-indie.intro: How to make films in New York on an indie budget, from director Nivedkrishna Thavarayil: the New York Film Academy, jugaad, cold DMs, the city as a free set, and the micro dramas he now directs for Canvas. Practical no-budget filmmaking advice, with a checklist for your first shoot and the mistakes to avoid.

ten-episodes-at-harvard-in-under-four-da.intro: Behind the scenes of Demo Day, a 10-episode web series shot at Harvard in under four days and directed by Nivedkrishna Thavarayil for Canvas. Two roommate founders, a real Harvard pitch as the finale, and no lead actor on the morning the crew left.
tags: how to shoot a web series

how-we-plan-a-micro-drama-in-a-day.intro: How Nivedkrishna Thavarayil plans a micro drama in a day: the AI production stack behind the 12+ short-form series he directed for Canvas across New York, Boston, Baltimore, San Francisco and Los Angeles. Planning in Directure AI, a Claude Code post-production pipeline, turning every shoot into ad creative, and what AI doesn't do.
tags: how to make a micro drama

why-i-broke-the-180-degree-rule.intro: Director Nivedkrishna Thavarayil on breaking the 180-degree rule in Agent X, his prison-cell interrogation scene at the New York Film Academy: one cell, one light, dolly track on both sides of the table, and a camera that switches sides when the power does. A short lesson in blocking and film grammar.
links: Watch the Agent X scene on YouTube

canvas-at-sf-and-la-tech-week.intro: What happened when Canvas went to SF Tech Week and LA Tech Week in October 2026: the Canvas launch party in San Francisco, The Hybrid Studio in Los Angeles, Oscar-winning editor Hemal Trivedi on stage, and the trailers for the micro dramas Nivedkrishna Thavarayil directed. What two rooms taught him about pitching stories to tech, with a checklist for small teams.
links: The Canvas launch party post on Instagram

fifteen-people-on-one-floor.intro: Nivedkrishna Thavarayil joined WLDD in Bangalore in January 2023, when the meme marketing agency was about fifteen people on one floor. What he made there, what a meme agency's early team taught him, three rules for content people want to share, and how WLDD went on to own ScoopWhoop.

what-the-popes-exorcist-taught-me-about-.intro: How a possession in a packed Indian cinema made The Pope's Exorcist go viral: Nivedkrishna Thavarayil on the Sony Pictures India campaign he worked on as a creative strategist at WLDD in 2023, covered by Hindustan Times and The Indian Express. Five lessons on virality, cultural fluency, memes and speed, and why most brands get it wrong.

hub-hype-and-hygiene.intro: Hub, hype and hygiene is the posting mix Nivedkrishna Thavarayil uses for every brand he runs, from film and FMCG campaigns at WLDD to cafes in New York. How to plan a week of social media posts without running out of ideas, a weekly template, how to measure each H, and the mistakes to avoid.

your-product-needs-a-format-not-an-ad.intro: Your product doesn't need an ad. It needs a format. Nivedkrishna Thavarayil on how Brick Lane Curry House turned its famous phaal, the curry Adam Richman took on in Man v. Food, into a creator challenge with no budget for paid creators. How to find your own format and treat creators as contestants, not billboards.

the-only-sales-strategy-i-have-ever-used.intro: Growvior, the software company Nivedkrishna Thavarayil co-founded with Agrajh AK, closed a $10,000 client without cold email, ads or a sales deck. The only sales strategy he has ever used: tell people what you do, pitch everything, and let your online presence pitch for you.
